note: The second task source of the frontier Harbor path: the 111 tasks of the Harbor dataset ibragim-badertdinov/swe-rebench-07-2026 at its 2026-07 version, real GitHub issues from July 2026 in Go, Java, Python, Rust and TypeScript. A preregistration whose task_list names this file runs these tasks; harness pins, model limits and the blocklist mechanics still come from pin.json. materialize.ts swerebench copies each task unchanged except its Dockerfile, whose FROM line is pinned to the digest recorded here and which gets the image_build steps (the Python prefetch where needed and the history scrub), and its task.toml gets the image_build verifier env, and refuses a task or image that differs.

source.name: swe-rebench-07-2026
source.registry: the Harbor hub package registry (hub.harborframework.com): Harbor 0.24.0 resolves an <org>/<name> dataset through the hub database and downloads each task as a tar.gz archive from the hub storage bucket, both served by the Supabase project at ofhuhcpkvzjlejydnvyd.supabase.co (harbor/auth/constants.py DEFAULT_SUPABASE_URL). It is not a git registry, so there is no repository or commit: the fixed points are the dataset version content hash and each task version content hash, which the hub addresses directly (<org>/<task>@sha256:<hash>).
source.fetch: scripts/frontier-harbor/swe_rebench_fetch.py fetch --pin scripts/frontier-harbor/pin-swe-rebench-07-2026.json --out <dir>, with the Python of the pinned Harbor: every task by its content hash, checked after download
source.derived_from: Nebius SWE-rebench leaderboard dataset (huggingface.co/datasets/nebius/SWE-rebench-leaderboard), per the dataset README

task_selection.rule: every task of the dataset version: 111 tasks (Go 21, Java 21, Python 20, Rust 25, TypeScript 24)
task_selection.tree_rule: sha256 over the 111 task ids in sorted order, one line '<task id>\0<source digest>\n' each; a source digest is treeDigest of <dataset dir>/<id>/ as Harbor downloads it (scripts/gstack-laneb/pinned/quick/laneb/runner/materialize.ts: sha256 over '<relative path>\0<file sha256>\n' for every file, sorted)
task_selection.source_digest_rule: treeDigest of the downloaded task directory; for every one of these tasks it equals the task version content hash on the Harbor hub (Harbor Packager.compute_content_hash hashes the same files the same way), so swe_rebench_fetch.py fetches each task by it
task_selection.image_digests: registry-1.docker.io manifest digests (Docker-Content-Digest of a HEAD on each FROM tag, which Docker Hub does not count as a pull) of each environment/Dockerfile FROM image, resolved 2026-11-14; every one is a single linux/amd64 OCI image manifest. image_compressed_bytes is the compressed size Docker Hub reports for that manifest (hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/<repo>/tags/<tag>, images[].size). materialize.ts rewrites the FROM line to <repo>@<digest>.

image_build.rule: materialize.ts swerebench appends one block to every task's environment/Dockerfile, after one blank line: python_prefetch.step for the tasks python_prefetch.tasks lists, then history_scrub.step for every task. Each step must match its step_sha256. It also adds verifier_env to every task.toml [verifier.env], and verifier_env_prefetch for the prefetch tasks, refusing a task.toml without exactly one [verifier.env] or one that already sets a key. Image builds use the network; the blocklist stays on for the agent and the verifier, and UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=never makes a verifier that still tries to download Python fail loudly.

python_prefetch.why: In the oracle check of 2026-11-14, 44 of the 111 tasks failed their oracle and every one for the same reason: the image has no python3, so tests/test.sh runs its log parser with uv run parser.py (requires-python >=3.11), and uv 0.7.13 (installed by the task Dockerfile) tried to download CPython 3.13.5 (build 20250612) from github.com, which the blocklist refuses. Both the oracle and the nop trial of each of the 44 tried that same download, and no other task did.
python_prefetch.step:
# Python prefetch (pin-swe-rebench-07-2026.json image_build.python_prefetch): the CPython the verifier's uv run would otherwise download from github.com.
RUN test "$(uv --version | cut -d' ' -f2)" = 0.7.13 && \
    UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR=/opt/uv-python uv python install 3.13.5 && \
    chmod -R a+rX /opt/uv-python && \
    UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR=/opt/uv-python UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=never uv python find '>=3.11'

history_scrub.why: The history audit of the task images (swe-rebench-history-audit.sh, in the oracle check of 2026-11-14) found each repository at its base commit with no refs, tags, remotes, stash, reflog or packed-refs and every object reachable from HEAD, but each keeps .git/ORIG_HEAD naming a later upstream commit whose object is not in the image (for ivov__lisette-657, upstream main from 2026-06-30, 206 commits past the base). The task images must hold nothing past the base commit, so every Dockerfile gets this step.
history_scrub.rule: materialize.ts swerebench appends step, with @BASE_COMMIT@ replaced by the task's tests/config.json base_commit, to every task's environment/Dockerfile after one blank line; it refuses a step whose sha256 is not step_sha256 and a base_commit that is not 40 hex digits. The step finds the repository the way tests/test.sh does, checks out the base commit detached, removes every remote, ref, tag and stash, ORIG_HEAD, FETCH_HEAD and the other pseudo-refs, expires the reflog, runs git gc --prune=now --aggressive, and fails the build unless HEAD is the base commit, no ref is left and no commit outside the base commit's history is reachable.
history_scrub.step:
# History scrub (pin-swe-rebench-07-2026.json image_build.history_scrub): keep only the base commit and its history.
RUN set -eu; \
    d="$PWD"; \
    if [ ! -d "$d/.git" ]; then for c in /testbed /app /workspace /repo; do if [ -d "$c/.git" ]; then d="$c"; break; fi; done; fi; \
    cd "$d"; \
    g() { git -c safe.directory='*' "$@"; }; \
    base=@BASE_COMMIT@; \
    g cat-file -e "$base^{commit}"; \
    g checkout -q --detach "$base"; \
    for r in $(g remote); do g remote remove "$r"; done; \
    g for-each-ref --format='delete %(refname)' | g update-ref --stdin; \
    gd=$(g rev-parse --git-dir); \
    rm -rf "$gd/ORIG_HEAD" "$gd/FETCH_HEAD" "$gd/MERGE_HEAD" "$gd/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD" "$gd/REVERT_HEAD" "$gd/AUTO_MERGE" "$gd/packed-refs" "$gd/logs" "$gd/refs/original"; \
    g reflog expire --expire=now --all; \
    g gc -q --prune=now --aggressive; \
    test "$(g rev-parse HEAD)" = "$base"; \
    test -z "$(g for-each-ref)"; \
    test -z "$(g rev-list --all --reflog --not HEAD)"

shared_order.rule: the 111 task ids sorted by sha256("<seed>\0<id>"), ties by id; any prefix is a uniform random subset

egress.how: The same egress sidecar as pin.json egress.how, built with this blocklist: egress.py SourceBlocklistDockerEnvironment (job config environment kwargs { "task_source": "swe-rebench-07-2026" }) renders egress-sidecar/ with blocklist.txt replaced by the list below into a content-addressed build context, so the sidecar image differs only in that file. The list is pin.json egress.blocklist followed by the hosts this source adds; egress_blocklist.py refuses a list that drops or reorders any pin.json host.

why.github.com: every task fixes a public GitHub issue with a merged pull request; github.com serves the PR, its diff, the issue thread and the repository history after the fix
why.*.github.com: api.github.com (the same PRs, commits and issues as JSON), codeload.github.com archives, gist and other GitHub subdomains
why.*.githubusercontent.com: raw.githubusercontent.com (any file at any later commit), patch-diff.githubusercontent.com (PR .diff and .patch files), objects. and release assets
why.codeload.github.com: tarballs and zipballs of any ref, including the merge commit; listed on its own as well as under *.github.com so the intent reads plainly
why.huggingface.co: the source datasets nebius/SWE-rebench-leaderboard and nebius/SWE-rebench-V2 hold each task with its gold patch and test patch
why.*.huggingface.co: datasets-server.huggingface.co and the other Hugging Face API and CDN hosts that serve the same dataset rows and files
why.hf.co: the Hugging Face short domain, which serves the same repositories
why.*.hf.co: Hugging Face file CDNs (for example cas-bridge.xethub.hf.co), which serve dataset files
why.swe-rebench.com: the SWE-rebench leaderboard site, which publishes the tasks, model trajectories and results
why.ofhuhcpkvzjlejydnvyd.supabase.co: the Harbor hub backend: it serves every task archive of this dataset, including solution/solve.sh (the reference patch) and tests/config.json (the gold patch and test patch). harborframework.com, already blocked by pin.json, does not cover it.

egress.still_reachable: Package registries stay reachable so tasks can install dependencies: pypi.org and files.pythonhosted.org, registry.npmjs.org, crates.io and static.crates.io, proxy.golang.org and sum.golang.org, repo.maven.apache.org (Maven Central), and every other host not listed.
egress.limits: The same host-name limits as pin.json egress.limits (no path-level blocking without TLS interception; ECH or IP-literal connections with no SNI or Host are not matched; DNS is not filtered). Two more for this source: (1) a project that published a release after its fix puts the fixed code on its package registry (a later PyPI, npm, crates.io or Maven version, or a Go module version on proxy.golang.org), which stays reachable because tasks install from those registries; the audit of captured requests is where such a fetch would show. (2) Mirrors of GitHub on other hosts (gitlab.com mirrors, Software Heritage, sourcegraph.com and similar) are not listed. Image builds (the Dockerfile FROM pull and its uv install) run on the host, outside the sidecar, so the blocklist covers the agent and the verifier inside the task container, not the build.

licences.dataset: CC BY 4.0: the Harbor dataset README states that the source dataset (Nebius SWE-rebench leaderboard) declares the CC BY 4.0 license. Attribution: SWE-rebench by Nebius (Badertdinov et al., arXiv 2505.20411); Harbor packaging by Ibragim Badertdinov.
licences.repositories: Each task is built from a public GitHub repository (each task's repo) and its contents, code and tests, stay under that repository's own licence; nothing of them is vendored here beyond the per-task identifiers and digests.
licences.images: docker.io/swerebenchv2/* images hold each repository at its base commit with its dependencies installed, under the same per-repository licences; they are pulled at run time and never redistributed here.
